newsitem.title: UK: HSBC says to merge Swiss operations.
newsitem.headline: HSBC says to merge Swiss operations.

text.p: HSBC Holdings Plc said on Tuesday it intends to merge its Swiss operations, subject to the approval of the Swiss Banking Commission.
The merged business will operate as Guyerzeller Bank AG, HSBC said in a statement.

Guyerzeller Bank AG will acquire the entire share capital of Trinkaus & Burkhardt's Swiss-incorporated subsidiary Trinkaus & Burkhardt (Schweiz) AG, HSBC said. In turn, Trinkaus & Burkhardt KGaA will purchase from HSBC's wholly-owned unit Midland Bank an indirect stake of some 16 percent in Guyerzeller Bank AG.
HSBC indirectly owns through Midland Bank about 73 percent of Dusseldorf-based Trinkaus & Burkhardt KGaA and some 75 percent of Zurich-based Guyerzeller Bank AG.
In Switzerland the two banks provide investment advice and asset management services to "high net worth individuals", HSBC said.

"Combining Trinkaus & Burkhardt's Swiss operation with our existing business will help reinforce our position as one of the top private banks in Switzerland, and gives us wider access to the German private banking market," Guyerzeller's chief executive Karl Preisig said in a statement.
HSBC said the transactions, whose value represents less than one percent of its group net assets, are expected to be completed by the end of the year.
HSBC Holdings, one the world's biggest banking and financial services organisations, had asset of about 237 billion pounds($388 billion)at the end of 1996. ($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
